related_questions.question: What are the warning signs of lymphoma?

text_blocks.snippet: The most common warning signs of lymphoma include painless swelling of lymph nodes (often in the neck, armpit, or groin), persistent fatigue, unexplained weight loss, and drenching night sweats. Other potential symptoms include fever, itching, shortness of breath, and abdominal pain or swelling.
snippet_highlighted_words: painless swelling of lymph nodes (often in the neck, armpit, or groin), persistent fatigue, unexplained weight loss, and drenching night sweats

text_blocks.snippet: More details on the warning signs:

list.title: Swollen lymph nodes:
list.snippet: These are often the first noticeable sign and can feel like lumps under the skin. They are usually painless, but can sometimes become painful, especially after drinking alcohol.

list.title: Fatigue:
list.snippet: Feeling unusually tired or exhausted, even after adequate rest, can be a sign.

list.title: Unexplained weight loss:
list.snippet: Losing 10% or more of your body weight over six months without trying to lose weight can be a warning sign.

list.title: Drenching night sweats:
list.snippet: Soaking the bedclothes with sweat, requiring a change of clothes or bedding, is another potential indicator.

list.title: Fever:
list.snippet: A persistent fever that is not caused by an infection can also be a symptom.

list.title: Other symptoms:
list.snippet: Itching, shortness of breath, cough, abdominal pain or swelling, and feeling full after eating small amounts of food can also be associated with lymphoma.

text_blocks.snippet: MALT lymphoma symptoms vary depending on where the cancer develops, but common signs include stomach upset, abdominal pain, weight loss, and fatigue. Other symptoms can include coughing, shortness of breath, lumps in the mouth or jaw, skin rashes, and eye problems.
snippet_highlighted_words: stomach upset, abdominal pain, weight loss, and fatigue

list.snippet: Gastric (Stomach) MALT Lymphoma: Indigestion, heartburn, stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, and unexplained weight loss.
Lung MALT Lymphoma: Persistent cough, shortness of breath, chest pain, and coughing up blood.
Salivary Gland MALT Lymphoma: Lumps in the mouth or jaw, or in front of the ear.
Eye MALT Lymphoma: Double vision, lumps or rashes on the eyelids, or a bulging eyeball.
Skin MALT Lymphoma: Pink or purplish patches on the skin.
Other Gastrointestinal Sites: Diarrhea, bloating, abdominal pain, and weight loss.
Thyroid MALT Lymphoma: A lump at the base of the neck, shortness of breath, trouble swallowing, hoarse voice, tiredness, and weight gain.

text_blocks.snippet: Fatigue and unexplained weight loss, Fever and night sweats (B symptoms), and Swelling or lumps in affected areas.

list.snippet: Some individuals with MALT lymphoma may not experience any noticeable symptoms, especially in the early stages, according to MD Anderson Cancer Center.
Symptoms can be similar to other conditions, so it's important to see a doctor for a proper diagnosis.
MALT lymphoma is often linked to chronic infections or autoimmune disorders, so it's helpful to discuss your medical history with your doctor.
